cases.reply: Comets are icy bodies that formed farther out in the solar system and grow a coma and tails when sunlight vaporizes their volatiles near perihelion; asteroids are dry, rocky-metallic leftovers, most of them orbiting in the main belt between Mars and Jupiter. Their sizes overlap, from a few meters to hundreds of kilometers, so composition and orbit are the real dividing lines rather than size. The boundary is blurry: some objects, like those in the Centaur population, behave like both.
